$comment: Hand-owned. This is the intent layer: figma-cli synthesises names like
'accent-9' and 'text-primary-5' by usage frequency, which are exact in
value but say nothing about meaning, and renumber whenever the design
changes. So we pin the VALUE and name it ourselves.
Every value here is verified against the live Figma palette on each
`npm run tokens:build`. If a value is retired or edited in Figma, the build
fails and names the token, rather than shipping a stale hex.
That check is only as good as the palette behind it, and `figma-cli
extract` does not descend into INSTANCE children: colours that only ever
occur inside an instance were missing from it entirely, so mapping them
failed as 'no longer exists in Figma' while they sat in plain sight on the
Meeting frame. figma-pull.ts now reads the fills back out of Figma and
completes the palette. See its readAllFillHexes.
Light theme only. Dark exists in the Figma for the Home frames and is
deferred; these names are deliberately semantic so a dark set can slot in
without touching a single component.
The color-call-* block is NOT that deferred dark theme. Meet's in-call
screen is dark whatever your theme, the way a video player is, so the call
is an always-dark SURFACE rather than a theme. Keeping it separate is what
lets the light/dark toggle stay deferred without the call wrongly following
it later. Values sampled from the Desktop / Meeting frame. See CLAUDE.md.
The color-call-panel-* block is the exception, and it is not a mistake: the
Chat and People panels are WHITE, floating on that black call. Verified by
pixel: the Light and Dark sections' Chat frames are identical (0 of 7720704
differ), so the white is the design in both and not a section artifact.
These are still call tokens, not theme tokens, for the same reason as the
block above - the panel is white whatever your theme, so the deferred toggle
must not reach it either.

$typography.$comment: Our role -> the Figma style key. Same reasoning as the colours: extract names the ramp body-2..body-7 by usage frequency, which says nothing about intent.
